turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because... well, recently I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt. I do art for a living, so I'm used to second-guessing my work, but this was different. I kept getting these really awful, unwanted thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. 

It was like, if I made just one wrong photo placement or picked the wrong color, it meant I didn't love her enough. I just couldn't brush them off like my normal creative doubts, and it really bothered me.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient reports recurrent, intrusive, and distressing unwanted thoughts about dishonoring their aunt that they could not brush off or dismiss.

turns.doctor_question: When these thoughts came up, did you feel driven to do something repeatedly to make sure you had not dishonored your aunt?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I did. Um, I would end up rereading the label text for the piece over and over. And I'd keep... just nudging the same objects around on my work table, or checking the layout photos repeatedly. I basically had to keep doing all that until things finally felt, I don't know, settled. 

It's really frustrating because part of me knows the piece is already fine, but I feel like I have to do it anyway, and I just end up losing a lot of good studio time.
